name: assembleContinuous
signature: export function assembleContinuous(parts: readonly EffectPart[], affects: LayerSelector, ctx: AbilityContext, env: PrimitiveEnv, note: string): ContinuousEffect | null
rules: CR 613.6 the affected set is locked when the effect starts applying
layerOrTiming: n/a - assembles the record layers.ts consumes
contract: Returns null when parts is empty. computeLayers already filters those, but returning one would burn an id and a timestamp on nothing.
The id is derived from env alone, so two clients replaying one log build the same effect list.
The timestamp is the caller-supplied env timestamp, which comes from state.version. Never a clock: the last anthem winning must mean the same thing on both screens.
provides is derived from the parts, not passed in, so a caller cannot forget it and quietly break CR 613.8 ordering.
fromAbility is left unset. These effects come from a resolved spell or ability and must outlive their source, which is exactly what the CR 613.6 note in layers.ts describes.

unlocks.source: supporting primitive for P01 and P02
